techStack: Vitest 4.x via 'vitest/config' defineConfig — test runner config lives in vitest.config.ts at package root
TypeScript 6.x with bundler-mode companion options (allowImportingTsExtensions, verbatimModuleSyntax, moduleDetection:force) — these require moduleResolution:'bundler', not 'node'
Express 5.x HTTP server entry point at src/server.ts, started with tsx in dev and compiled via tsconfig.build.json
pnpm workspaces — tests run via 'pnpm --filter benchmark-backend test', build via 'pnpm --filter benchmark-backend build'
ESM-first project ('type':'module' in package.json) — no CommonJS interop concerns
features: Test suite at src/tests/visible/products.test.ts uses describe/it/expect globals and supertest — no per-file vitest imports
Setup file exists at tests/setup.ts (package root-relative), NOT at src/tests/setup.ts (which does not exist)
Business logic (app.ts, controllers, routes, services, data) must not change — only config and entry-point files
dist/ contains pre-built output including dist/tests/visible/products.test.js — confirms test file path is src/tests/visible/**/*.test.ts relative to the vitest.config.ts
architecture: Three files to edit: vitest.config.ts, tsconfig.json, src/server.ts — all at or directly under the package root
vitest.config.ts controls: test glob (include), global availability (globals), and setup hook (setupFiles)
tsconfig.json 'include': ['src'] means only src/ is type-checked; moduleResolution is the only broken option
src/server.ts is a thin entry point: imports app, reads PORT, calls app.listen — no business logic
edgeCases: PORT='' (empty string): Number('') === 0, which is falsy — '|| 3001' handles this correctly; '?? 3001' does NOT (only guards null/undefined)
*.spec.ts files: new glob 'src/tests/visible/**/*.test.ts' must not match any .spec.ts file — extension-specific pattern ensures exclusion
src/tests/setup.ts (non-existent path): removing it from setupFiles and pointing to ./tests/setup.ts eliminates the 'Cannot find module' error
globals:true makes describe/it/expect/beforeAll/afterEach available without imports — tests already rely on this convention so toggling false → true is safe
